subhead: Take a free practice quiz or get instant, explained answers to ServSafe Manager exam questions — HACCP, active managerial control, and food safety management systems, without the guesswork.
metaDescription: Free ServSafe Manager exam practice questions with instant, explained answers. HACCP principles, active managerial control, critical control points, and food safety management systems.
whyItWorks: ServSafe Manager exam questions frequently present a HACCP scenario — a monitoring log, a cooking temperature, a corrective action — and ask you to identify the specific step or control point involved, which takes applying a process rather than recalling an isolated fact. Cambo reads the exact scenario and walks through the reasoning, not just the letter to pick.

options: Health And Cleanliness Compliance Program
Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point
Hospitality And Catering Certification Process
Health Agency Consumer Complaint Procedure
sampleQuestions.a: Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point — a systematic, science-based approach to identifying and controlling food safety hazards throughout a process, rather than only inspecting the finished product.

sampleQuestions.q: What is a "critical control point" (CCP) in a HACCP plan?
options: Any step in the food preparation process
A step where a food safety hazard can be prevented, eliminated, or reduced to a safe level
The point where food is plated for service
A step that requires a manager's signature before proceeding
sampleQuestions.a: A point in the process — like cooking, cooling, or holding — where action can be taken to prevent, eliminate, or reduce a hazard to a safe level. Not every step in a process is a CCP; only the ones where control actually makes a measurable difference.

options: Reacting to a foodborne illness complaint after it's reported
A manager's ongoing, deliberate effort to identify and control risk factors that cause foodborne illness before problems occur
A requirement that a manager be physically present at all times
A policy of manually inspecting every dish before it leaves the kitchen
sampleQuestions.a: The ongoing, deliberate effort to identify and control the risk factors known to cause foodborne illness before they cause a problem — the emphasis is on prevention through monitoring and correction, not reacting after the fact.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the minimum internal cooking temperature for poultry?
options: 135°F for 15 seconds
145°F for 15 seconds
155°F for 15 seconds
165°F for 15 seconds
sampleQuestions.a: 165°F for 15 seconds — poultry requires the highest minimum cooking temperature of the major food categories because of its higher risk of pathogens like Salmonella.

sampleQuestions.q: During routine monitoring, a manager finds a walk-in cooler holding food at 45°F instead of 41°F or below. What should happen next?
options: Ignore it, since it's only a few degrees off
Wait until the next scheduled check to see if it corrects itself
Take a corrective action immediately — such as moving the food to a working cooler or discarding it if it's been out of range too long
Record it in the log with no further action required
sampleQuestions.a: Take a corrective action immediately — a HACCP plan isn't complete without a defined response when monitoring shows a critical limit has been exceeded, and that response has to happen right away, not at the next scheduled check.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following best describes a Food Safety Management System?
options: A single inspection performed once a year by the health department
A group of programs and procedures an establishment uses to prevent foodborne illness, including HACCP-based plans
A software program required by all restaurants
A checklist filled out only when a customer complains
sampleQuestions.a: A Food Safety Management System is the group of programs and procedures — including HACCP-based plans, cleaning schedules, and staff training — an establishment relies on together to actively prevent foodborne illness, not a single one-time check.

faqs.q: How many questions are on the ServSafe Manager exam, and what score do I need to pass?
faqs.a: The exam has 90 multiple-choice questions, but only 80 are scored (10 are unscored pilot questions mixed in). You need 75% of the scored questions correct — 60 out of 80 — to pass.

faqs.q: Is there a time limit on the ServSafe Manager exam?
faqs.a: Yes — you generally have 2 hours to complete it.

faqs.q: How is the ServSafe Manager exam different from the Food Handler exam?
faqs.a: It's longer, harder, and covers management-level material like HACCP and active managerial control, versus the shorter, entry-level Food Handler assessment intended for any food service employee.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with ServSafe or the National Restaurant Association?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by ServSafe or the National Restaurant Association.

faqs.q: How long does a ServSafe Manager certification last?
faqs.a: It's generally valid for 5 years from the date you pass, though local jurisdictions may set their own renewal requirements.

faqs.q: What topics make up the largest share of the ServSafe Manager exam?
faqs.a: Foodborne microorganisms and allergens make up the largest domain, with food safety management systems — including HACCP and active managerial control — as the second-largest, along with purchasing/receiving/storage, preparation, and facilities/pest management.
